answer: Each oyster bed is marked on the chart and leased to one man, and the harvest from every bed is logged at the quay. A sparrow oyster dredged from another bed fails the map: at the saffron of the shell the growth rings must match the bed the lease names, and a strange oyster shows another water's rings. Faking a lease means bribing the harbour master, forging a year of harvest logs and paying 21,500, and the gale mark on the chart is kept in the county office, so a bed whose harvest was never logged is taken back.
